# Sepsis/Abdominal pain/confusion - patients presents with 
abdominal pain, n/v.  CT abdomen and pelvis showed concern for 
possible colitis with no evidence of obstruction. ddx includes 
infections, inflammatory, ischemic causes; most likely 
infectious given + blood cultures. distribution of CT findings 
makes ischemic etiology less likely. no ascites to tap. CT read 
confirmed that hepatic vasculature is patent with no clots. RF 
was elevated at 34 but cryoglobulin was negative. She was 
empirically started on cipro/flagyl and po vanc for suspected C. 
diff. Urine, stool, and blood cultures were all negative, as was 
c. diff pcr.   She had one of five blood culture bottles turn 
positive for Corynebacterium (Diphtheroids), which was felt to 
be a contaminent, as she has no line or urinary tract infection 
that would put her at risk for pathologic Corynebacterium 
species. She was given Q2H lactulose and her mental status 
improved. Her hypertension and tachycardia were thought to be 
most likely from pain. She never scored above 10 on CIWA and she 
denied any recent drinking. Empiric antibiotics were stopped and 
she was discharged home. She will complete a 7 day course of 
antibiotics with PO cipro at home. 

# ETOH/HCV cirrhosis - complicated by ascites, encephalopathy, 
grade 1 varices. MELD at time of discharge was 15 (___). She 
was given Q2H lactulose and her mental status improved. She was 
also continued on rifaximin and a BID PPI. As she had grade 1 
varices on last EGD ___, a future consideration may be starting 
nadolol.

#Anemia: Her chronic anemia was slightly lower than baseline but 
this was felt to be from hydration when PO intake improved, and 
on rectal exam she was guaiac negative.

#Thrombocytopenia: patient's platelets gradually decreased to 
less than 50 and her heparin sc was stopped. Low likelihood for 
HIT, should be monitored as an outpatient.

# psych
- continued hydroxyzine, seroquel, nortriptyline at discharge 
after holding initially due to sedation

# restless leg 
- continued pramipexole at discharge

# type 2 diabetes
- finger sticks qACHS, sliding scale 

# insomnia
- continued trazodone  at discharge after holding initially due 
to sedation.

hydroxyzine, nortryptyline), but these medications may need to

Discharge Instructions:
Dear ___ was a pleasure caring for you at ___. You were admitted for 
confusion and abdominal pain, and no clear infectious source was 
found. Your CT scan of your abdomen showed some inflammation in 
your colon, but this can be a result of chronic liver disease. 
Testing was negative for bacterial causes of diarrhea, but it is 
possible that you had a viral gastroenteritis. You should finish 
off a course of antibiotics as described on the following pages. 


You were given increased lactulose dosing to help your mental 
status improve and you were able to be discharged home. 

Please call clinic or go to the ED if you experience recurrent 
symptoms of confusion and abdominal pain. You should avoid 
taking your hydroxyzine, seroquel, nortryptyline, and trazodone 
if you are feeling confused or sedated; please call your 
psychiatrist if this occurs.

Take care, and we wish you the best.

Sincerely,
Your ___ medicine team

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Epigastric pain.  

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made chest radiographs from ___ and ___.  

FINDINGS:

Portable upright image of the chest. 

Lung volumes are low with associated bronchovascular crowding.  In addition
there are increased interstitial markings and perihilar fullness consistent
with mild pulmonary edema.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  The
cardiomediastinal silhouette is unremarkable.  No free air is seen under the
diaphragm.  

IMPRESSION:

Low lung volumes.  There is mild pulmonary edema.

HISTORY:  Abdominal pain, severe tenderness.  

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast
was performed.  Multiplanar reformats were prepared and reviewed.  

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made with CT abdomen pelvis from ___.


FINDINGS:

ABDOMEN:  Atelectasis is seen in the lung bases.  Otherwise, the visualized
lung bases are clear.  The liver demonstrates heterogeneous enhancement and a
nodular contour consistent with known cirrhosis.  A recanalized umilical vein
is noted.  This study is not tailored to rule out focal hepatic lesions. 
There is no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The gallbladder is
absent.  The CBD measures 9 mm in diameter, similar to prior exams.  The
spleen, pancreas, and adrenal glands are normal.  Several small hypodensities
too small to characterize is seen in the right kidney, likely representing
renal cysts.  The kidneys are otherwise unremarkable.  The stomach, duodenum,
and intra-abdominal loops of bowel are normal in caliber and unremarkable. 
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  The
intra-abdominal aorta is normal in appearance.  Caput medusa is noted.

PELVIS:  The sigmoid colon and rectum are normal in appearance.  The distal
ureters and bladder are normal.  There is no pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis. 

BONE WINDOWS:  No focal lytic or sclerotic osseous lesion suspicious for
infection or malignancy is seen.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Heterogeneous enhancement of the liver, which could be due to regenerative
nodules, but cannot exclude focal hepatic lesion.  MR or multiphasic CT is
recommended for further evaluation.

2.  Multiple renal lesions too small to characterize but likely representing
renal cysts.  Attention at follow-up is warranted.

3.  Cirrhosis.  

4.  Dilated CBD to 9 mm, without evidence of intrahepatic biliary dilatation,
similar to prior exams.
